references.text: The Lord was with Joseph, and he became a successful man. The parallel to 39:21 is direct: God's presence followed Joseph from Potiphar's house to the prison.
Psalm 105 retells Joseph's story: he was sold as a slave, put in iron chains, until the Lord's word came true. God was with him through his trials.
'He caused them to find mercy with all who held them captive.' This directly reflects how God gave Joseph favor in the eyes of the prison warden.
God's promise to be with His people through water and fire illustrates the same principle: God's faithful presence in difficult circumstances, as Joseph experienced in prison.
'I will not leave you nor forsake you.' God's promise of faithful presence is reflected in His ongoing care for Joseph in prison.
'When the Lord delights in a man's ways, He makes even his enemies be at peace with him.' This illustrates how God gave Joseph favor even with the prison warden.
Both verses document how God's presence with Joseph results in him finding favor with people across various life situations.
This is a direct narrative link showing the cause-and-effect relationship: God's presence leads to goodwill from the Egyptian.
A theological parallel showing how God's mercy is manifested through human agents in both history and Jesus' parables.
This verse shows the consequence of the source verse's event: God's presence with Joseph brings blessing over the entire prison.
This verse gives the human observation that confirms the divine reality described in the source verse.
